rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Measles is highly contagious and vaccine preventable.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Measles is a notifiable disease in England and Wales.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Health professionals should notify suspected cases to the local health protection team.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Public-health guidance covers assessment of cases, contacts and transmission risk.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Healthcare settings should check patient and staff vaccination status.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Two documented MMR doses are used as evidence of routine vaccine protection.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Cases should be excluded from nursery, education or work until four full days after rash onset.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Travel-linked cases require coordinated reporting and contact-tracing arrangements.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: Measles risk depends on vaccination, infectious timing, contact intensity, setting, age, immune status, travel and local transmission.

rows.source: UKHSA measles management and surveillance
rows.verified: UKHSA measles evidence is case-, contact-, vaccine-, setting-, geography- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: UKHSA guidance supports risk assessment and categorisation of contacts of confirmed mpox cases.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: Contact categories determine appropriate public-health follow-up and isolation advice.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: Information sheets are provided for medium- and high-risk contacts.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: UKHSA maintains separate resources for diagnosis, case management, vaccination and surveillance.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: Healthcare providers should conduct competent local risk assessments where mpox may be encountered.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: Suspected cases can require discussion with infection specialists and UKHSA services.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: Contacts who develop compatible symptoms should follow the advice supplied by health-protection teams.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: Event planning may include contact-management arrangements and post-event surveillance.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: Mpox risk depends on viral clade, contact type, exposure route, symptoms, setting, immunity, vaccination and response timing.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case and contact management
rows.verified: UKHSA mpox evidence is case-, contact-, clade-, setting-, vaccine- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
